dataset: Applicants' reported results per programme: 指南者留学 published cases, the GradCafe survey, Chinese universities' 飞跃手册, 金吉列留学 case articles, 新东方 slides of Kaplan Singapore graduates' offers

compass.name: 指南者留学 case library
compass.note: The agency's published admission cases of its own clients: chosen by it, mostly mainland Chinese applicants, admits only.

gradcafe.name: GradCafe admissions survey
gradcafe.note: Applicants' own reports, mostly to North American programmes: admits, rejections and waiting lists, with GPA and GRE where given.

feiyue.name: 飞跃手册 (university handbooks)
feiyue.note: Graduates' own accounts of all their applications (南方科技大学, 海南大学, 福州大学), admits and rejections.

jjl.name: 金吉列留学 case articles
jjl.note: The agency's published success stories: chosen to advertise, often a modest GPA's success, nearly all admits.

xdf.name: 新东方 Kaplan Singapore progression cases
xdf.note: The agency's slides of Kaplan Singapore graduates' master's offers (UCD, Northumbria and Murdoch degrees), each with the offer letter: chosen to advertise, admits only. Supplied as a PDF and transcribed by hand; names left out.

notes: Reported results, not the programmes' own figures: who chose to report, and what an agency chose to publish. Rejections are counted apart from admits.

GPA on the 4-point scale: four: reported on the 4-point scale; four-three: 4.3-point scale: anything above an A (4.0) counted as 4.0; five-cn: 5-point GPA (e.g. Nanjing, Tongji): 45 + 10 × GPA as a percentage, as Tongji University's own table gives (5 = 95, 4 = 85, 3 = 75), then Peking University's rule; percent-cn: percentage mark, converted with Peking University's rule GPA = 4 − 3(100 − X)²/1600; uk-mark: UK percentage mark (Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool's and Nottingham Ningbo's marks too), converted with the commonly cited bands (First 3.7–4.0, 2:1 3.3–3.6, 2:2 about 2.7, Third about 2.0); au-seven: Australian 7-point GPA, put on the UK scale with UK universities' published equivalences (7 a First, 6 a 2:1, 5 a 2:2), then the UK bands; au-mark: Australian average mark, put on the UK scale with UK universities' published equivalences (80% a First, 70% a 2:1, 65% a 2:2), then the UK bands; korea: 4.5-point scale, scaled by 4/4.5; ucd-4.2: University College Dublin's 4.2-point GPA: its class by UCD's own table (First 3.68–4.20, 2:1 3.08–3.67, 2:2 2.48–3.07, Pass 2.00–2.47), then the UK bands (First 3.7–4.0, 2:1 3.3–3.6, 2:2 2.7, Pass 2.0), straight-line within a class.

GMAT: each reported score put on the Focus Edition scale with GMAC's concordance table (a score ending in 5 read as a Focus Edition score, any other as a 10th Edition score: Kaplan 360++'s rule), then the median taken (edition "focus").

First degrees in tiers A, B and C (lib/tiers.ts): mainland China by the University of Cambridge's Group A and Group B lists (any other mainland institution C; a campus or faculty as its university; a combined name by its best part); everywhere else, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan included, the QS World University Rankings 2027 on Kaplan 360++'s rule (rank value 120 or better A, 121 to 300 B, 301 or below or not ranked C); a Sino-foreign university as its awarding university; a Singapore private school's degree as C (QS 301+ or unranked), whatever the awarding university. gpaByTier: n, p25, median, p75 and p90 of each tier's GPAs, for a tier with at least 5. groups: the six groups used before (985, 211, other mainland universities by the agency's category; overseas by QS band: top 50, 51–300, below or unranked), kept as details.

Reports are linked to a programme only when Claude was sure the name is the same programme (新东方's offers by hand, from the offer letters); reports from before 2022-01-01 are left out; programmes with fewer than 5 reported admits and rejections get no summary. Flags: gpaWide (middle 80% across 0.8 or more on the 4-point scale, or middle half across 0.4), ieltsWide (middle 80% across 1.5 bands), sourcesDiffer (sources' median GPAs 0.3 or more apart), rejectedHigher (rejected applicants' median GPA at or above admitted ones'), few (under 10 admits).
